extracted.intended_audience: readers of Don Quixote; students/analysts of literature and historical/fictive governance advice
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and summarize the norms, maxims, and administrative rules embedded in this Don Quixote passage (advice to the governor Sancho Panza and Sancho's ordinances). Useful for literary analysis of fictional governance or historical ideas of office-holding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dress appropriately to office
rubrics_metrics.description: Dress well; a stick dressed up does not look like a stick; array thyself in the apparel thy office requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don Quixote cautions Sancho not to rely on personal taste for dress but to wear neat, handsome apparel appropriate to the dignity of his office (not necessarily extravagant trinkets, but a suitable, respectable appearance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be civil to all
rubrics_metrics.description: To win the good-will of the people thou governest one thing thou must do is to be civil to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Politeness and civility are presented as a primary means to obtain popular goodwill and legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure abundant food for populace
rubrics_metrics.description: Take care that food be abundant, for there is nothing that vexes the heart of the poor more than hunger and high prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material provisioning (affordable food) is a core responsibility of governance; failure undermines authority and popular contentment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make few, enforceable proclamations
rubrics_metrics.description: Make not many proclamations; but those thou makest take care that they be good ones, and above all that they be observed and carried out; proclamations that are not observed are the same as if they did not exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clarity and enforceability of public decrees; hollow or unenforced proclamations erode authority and invite contempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a father to virtue and stepfather to vice
rubrics_metrics.description: Be a father to virtue and a stepfather to vice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively support and encourage virtuous behavior while discouraging vice—balance benevolence with corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe moderation between strictness and leniency
rubrics_metrics.description: Be not always strict, nor yet always lenient, but observe a mean between these two extremes, for in that is the aim of wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance requires calibrated judgment; neither extreme severity nor perpetual indulgence is wise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain visible presence in key public places
rubrics_metrics.description: Visit the gaols, the slaughter-houses, and the market-places; for the presence of the governor is of great importance in such places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal visitation reassures prisoners, restrains dishonest traders (butchers, market-women), and signals active oversight to the populace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid apparent personal vices
rubrics_metrics.description: Let it not be seen that thou art (even if perchance thou art) covetous, a follower of women, or a glutton; for when the people become aware of thy special weakness they will bring their batteries to bear upon thee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly visible personal weaknesses invite exploitation and undermine authority; cultivate a reputation of moderation and probity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsider and follow given counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and reconsider, con and con over again the advices and the instructions I gave thee before thy departure hence to thy government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberation and repeated reflection on sound counsel are recommended as practical aids for avoiding error in office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show gratitude to benefactors
rubrics_metrics.description: Write to thy lord and lady and show thyself grateful to them, for ingratitude is the daughter of pride.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain respectful relations with patrons and hosts; gratitude sustains reciprocal support and signals good character.

rubrics_metrics.name: In cases of doubt, lean to mercy
rubrics_metrics.description: When there was any doubt about the justice of a case I should lean to mercy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sancho applies this precept in a knotty legal puzzle: when arguments for conviction and acquittal are balanced, favor clemency. Presented as a practical judicial maxim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer doing good when arguments are balanced
rubrics_metrics.description: As the arguments for condemning him and for absolving him are exactly balanced, they should let him pass freely, as it is always more praiseworthy to do good than to do evil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When legal or moral considerations are evenly balanced, choose the action that effects good (mercy) rather than harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid corruption and taking bribes
rubrics_metrics.description: So far I have not handled any dues or taken any bribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sancho notes his practice of not taking bribes as a mark of upright administration; personal integrity is implied as a governance standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confiscate adulterated goods and punish vendors
rubrics_metrics.description: He confiscated the whole for the children of the charity-school, and he sentenced her not to come into the market-place for a fortnight (vendor who mixed old rotten nuts with new).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sancho enforces market honesty by seizure of adulterated products and temporary exclusion from trading; protecting consumers—especially the poor—is part of just governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban provision-hucksters (restrict itinerant profiteers)
rubrics_metrics.description: He ordained that there were to be no provision hucksters in the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibiting certain itinerant merchants is intended to curb unscrupulous commercial practices that harm consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require wine origin declaration and price differentiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Men might import wine into it from any place they pleased, provided they declared the quarter it came from, so that a price might be put upon it according to its quality, reputation, and the estimation it was held in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about provenance allows market-based valuation and consumer protection; labeling supports honest trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punish wine adulteration severely
rubrics_metrics.description: He that watered his wine, or changed the name, was to forfeit his life for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sancho prescribes draconian punishment for adulterating wine or mislabeling origin—underscoring the seriousness he attaches to market honesty (extreme as presented in the fiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix servants' wages to curb excesses
rubrics_metrics.description: He established a fixed rate for servants’ wages, which were becoming recklessly exorbitant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wage-setting is used as an administrative tool to control labor costs and perceived excesses; a regulatory intervention into local labor markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalize public performance of lewd songs
rubrics_metrics.description: He laid extremely heavy penalties upon those who sang lewd or loose songs either by day or night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral regulation of public speech/entertainment is part of his ordinance—aimed at public decency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require evidence for miraculous claims sung by blind minstrels
rubrics_metrics.description: He decreed that no blind man should sing of any miracle in verse, unless he could produce authentic evidence that it was true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule demands verification for sensational or miraculous public claims, discouraging fabrication and protecting truthfulness in popular narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an alguacil to verify poverty claims
rubrics_metrics.description: He established and created an alguacil of the poor, not to harass them, but to examine them and see whether they really were so; for many a sturdy thief or drunkard goes about under cover of a make-believe crippled limb or a sham sore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional verification to distinguish genuine paupers from impostors; intended to target fraud and ensure aid reaches the truly needy.
